userPrompt: Tasks spend as few turns as they can before doing the work. The spec-reading default tells a task to read only the compiled reference the prompt links to and what those pages link to that the change actually depends on, not to survey the spec first, and never to read a reference page already given to it as a slice in the prompt. The understanding file is written once, after the reading and before the first change, and rewritten only when a constraint in it turns out to be wrong, never after every page read. The defaults ask for a final reply of a few sentences saying what changed, not a recap of the work.
systemPrompt:
We're working in a project whose spec is compiled to .claude/reference, which is where to read it. Each prompt starts with a <task-instructions> block saying what that prompt is for and what it may change. Follow the block at the top of the prompt you are answering; an earlier prompt's block no longer applies.

Its spec's Piton source, in ./spec, is only where edits to the spec go.

Read the spec from its compiled reference under .claude/reference, where inheritance, expressions, and links are already resolved, or, for one thing, from what `piton slice` prints for it with this harness's adapter.

Never read the .pi source under ./spec to learn what the spec says; that is only where edits to the spec go.

Before executing anything, read the spec it touches. Links to .claude/reference/... in the prompt are the spec for what they name. Read each one you need before changing anything it covers. Don't re-read something you've already read.
instructions:
We're working on both the spec and the code, as a chain. This first step changes the spec only, located in ./spec; the code is changed in the next step.

Write the spec so it describes the application as it should be once the prompt is met, and constrains the code. Once you finish, the spec will be built and the same prompt sent to a coding agent, with your reply, to change the code to match it; so end your reply by saying what you changed in the spec and which anchors the code should follow.

When the work is about Suspense, its modes, its prompts, or its questions, or you are to write a prompt or a question for the user, first read .suspense/suspense-fluency.md once in this conversation, unless you already have: it is how Suspense works.

Before creating or editing any .pi file, read .suspense/fluency.md once in this conversation, unless you already have: it is how Piton is written.

Open a .pi file only to change it. Once you have changed the spec, run `piton check` and fix every error it reports, then run `piton build` and check the result in the refreshed reference under .claude/reference, not by reading the source again. Never finish with a spec that `piton check` or `piton build` reports errors in.

Before changing anything, write the constraints this task must meet to .suspense/history/1791485035-Prompt_81f60e02b63f82e2.understanding.md, and keep it current as you read more of the spec. It is a Markdown list and nothing else: one line per constraint, at most twelve, each a single short, specific statement of what must be true, written as a link to the compiled reference file it comes from, such as `- [The chain tab has no bottom border in combined mode](.claude/reference/scope/prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chain)`. Only list what the spec says; leave out anything you are deciding yourself. Replace a constraint when you learn it was wrong rather than adding another.

content.text:
I rewrote the default prompts so tasks read less before they start, write their constraints once, and end with a short reply. `piton check` reports no problems and `piton build` wrote 81 files.

## What changed in the spec

All edits are in `spec/scope/prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.pi`, under `#defaults`.

- **Spec-reading default:** its last paragraph now tells a task to:
  - read the reference pages the prompt links to, then only the pages those link to that the change depends on;
  - not survey the spec, list its folders or search it first;
  - never read a page the prompt already gives it as a slice, or anything it has already read.
- **Understanding-file paragraph** (Code, Chain and Spec defaults): the file is written once, after reading and before the first change, and rewritten only when a constraint in it turns out to be wrong, never after each page read. It used to say to write it before changing anything and keep it current while reading.
- **Short final reply (new):** the Code, Chain, Spec and Ask defaults end by asking for "a reply of a few sentences saying what changed, or for a question, the answer, not a recap of the work or of what you read."
- **Summary sentence:** a sentence after the defaults states the goal: as few turns as possible before the work starts.

**Existing projects won't pick this up on their own.** The spec already says a project keeps its saved prompts when a default changes. Reset the prompts in Settings to get the new defaults; new projects get them automatically.

The constraints are in `.suspense/history/1791485035-Prompt_81f60e02b63f82e2.understanding.md`.

## Anchors the code should follow
- `ModeSystemPromptsScope` `#defaults`: update `spec-reading.md`, `code.md`, `combined.md`, `spec.md` and `ask.md` in this repository's `.suspense/system-prompts`. The built-in defaults are taken from those files.
